title.narrative: Increased capacity of Member States to develop and implement effective and efficient labour market programmes and services to support transitions, including through employment-intensive investment programmes

description.narrative: The focus of this Global Product is to facilitate knowledge development and dissemination, guidance and capacity development, and evidence-based action to support efficient and effective transitions in a rapidly changing labour market. It will do so by developing a comprehensive and user-oriented set of studies, research, tools and guidelines on labour market programmes, employment-intensive investment programmes and employment services to facilitate inclusive transitions and the implementation of innovative approaches, including South–South learning, knowledge development and dissemination. It will also assess the outcomes of labour market programmes and create a repository of good practices to support constituents at country level as well as other stakeholders. As a standards-based organization, the ILO will promote in this policy area the ratification and implementation of the Employment Services Convention, 1948 (No.88) and the Private Employment Agencies Convention, 1997 (No.181) under the ongoing global campaign with a view to promoting more efficient and affective functioning of labour markets as they grapple with multiple crises. Moreover, it will strengthen the capacity of public and private national partners in collaboration with the Turin Centre and other organizations through global, regional or national customized capacity development initiatives. To ensure broad outreach and impact, the ILO will strengthen partnerships for more effective and coherent programmes and employment services, including employment-intensive employment programmes, across regions, including through cooperation with global and regional specialised organizations, private sector and UN agencies with a stronger and principal role for social partners on work-related policy matters, as well as with international financial institutions, multilateral partners and donors to increase the employment impact of their programmes and projects.
